mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) indicates accommodative monetary policy, which reduces the discount rate for equity valuation and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS remains below 0.5% for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods, or the Rank IC over 5-year rolling windows is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 7.0% and remains below this threshold for two consecutive months, it signals a strengthening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 7.0% and stays below for 2 months
failure_condition: Unemployment rate drops below 7.0% for two consecutive months but S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of such instances, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicate robust demand and supply chain health, which together signal strong economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST and INDPRO both rise for two consecutive months but S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of such cases, or the interaction term's Rank IC is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: In low-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL < 2.0%), a monthly rise in CPIAUCSL above 2.0% signals the end of deflationary pressures and the start of a mild inflationary cycle, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where CPIAUCSL < 2.0%, a rise above 2.0% is followed by negative 60-day S&P 500 returns in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average indicates strong consumer demand for housing, which correlates with rising consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST remains above its 12-month moving average for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of such periods, or the Rank IC over 4-year windows is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly job growth (PAYEMS) exceeds 200,000 new jobs, it signals a robust labor market that increases disposable income and consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS exceeds 200,000 in a month but S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of such months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) signal a coordinated monetary easing and labor market improvement, which together drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary easing with labor market improvement
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS declines and UNRATE falls simultaneously for two consecutive months but S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of such instances, or the interaction term's Rank IC is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: In manufacturing expansion regimes (INDPRO > 100), a sustained rise in industrial production above its 3-month moving average signals robust supply chain activity and strong economic growth, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO > 100 and INDPRO rises above its 3-month moving average for two consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of such cases, or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.02.
